newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown - economic recovery unbalanced.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown - economic recovery unbalanced.

text.p: Britain's economic recovery is an unbalanced one, opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Friday.

"There is now a growing unease that in the present cycle we are in danger of repeating the pattern seen in previous recoveries - that we have, essentially an unbalanced recovery," he told a business conference in London.
He said investment has been slower to respond in this economic recovery than in any other this century.
Brown said that by the equivalent stage of the 1980s economic cycle, investment had increased by 14 percent. In the 1970s upswing, it had grown by 21 percent.
"Today, in the 90s, we find ourselves with a level of manufacturing investment lower than at the trough of the recession, and falling again," he said.
He said manufacturing investment had fallen by 16 percent over the last year.
"Unless we tackle this problem the consequences will be profound because the result will continue to be slower growth and inflationary pressures," Brown said.
Brown reiterated his pledges to set a target for "low and stable inflation" and to establish a new monetary policy committee for the Bank of England, once Labour is in government.
"In the global economy, policies for economic management must recognise that low inflation is a precondition of sustainable growth," he said.
"I am determined to create a platform for stability by implementing credible anti-inflationary policies which convince people that they can expect stable non-inflationary growth."
